claims.text: The initial stainless steel has a native, unmodified surface that includes an inherent passive oxide layer.
A nanocrystalline ceramic coating can be applied to stainless steel using physical vapor deposition.
PVD deposition of a nanocrystalline ceramic coating improves the corrosion resistance of stainless steel compared with unmodified stainless steel.
The proposed improvement applies under chloride-rich conditions.
The proposed improvement applies at elevated temperatures representative of severe industrial environments.
The coating forms a robust, low-permeability ceramic barrier.
The ceramic coating modifies the surface composition of the stainless steel.
The nanocrystalline ceramic layer acts as a physical barrier to corrosive agents.
The ceramic layer reduces diffusion of chloride ions to the underlying metal.
Reduced transport of corrosive agents to the metal mitigates corrosion processes that compromise stainless-steel integrity.
The coated stainless steel will exhibit a significant reduction in corrosion rate relative to untreated stainless steel under identical extreme conditions.
Performance may vary when corrosive species or temperatures differ from the simulated severe environments.
The precise quantitative reduction in corrosion rate is unknown and requires systematic testing.
